   180	def pauliToLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) (z : PauliSpace P) :
   181	    LdSpace P.toLdParams :=
   182	  fun i => match i with
   183	  | .inl (.inl j) => pauliPointBlock W z j
   184	  | .inl (.inr _) => pauliScalarBlock z
   185	  | .inr j => pauliDirectionBlock z j
   186	
   187	/-- Embed a low-degree vector into the basis-selected Pauli blocks, clearing the
   188	other basis and the two `r` registers.  This is Lean-only coordinate plumbing
   189	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   190	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   191	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   192	-/
   193	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   194	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=
   195	  fun i => match i with
   196	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   197	      match W with
   198	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   199	      | .Z => 0
   200	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   201	      match W with
   202	      | .X => 0
   203	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))
   204	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => u (.inl (.inr ()))
   205	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   206	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   207	  | .inr _ => 0
   208	
   209	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from
   210	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper

430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   431	-/
   432	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   433	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   434	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=
   435	  fixedBinTrace P.model
   436	    (dotProduct (rX • indicatorVec uX) (rZ • indicatorVec uZ))
   437	
   438	/-- The commutation bit attached to a full Pauli ambient question, from
   439	`eq:gamma-value` in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   440	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   441	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.
   442	-/
   443	noncomputable def pauliPairGamma (P : AdmissibleParams) (z : PauliSpace P) : ZMod 2 :=
   444	  gammaValue P (pauliXBlock z) (pauliZBlock z)
   445	    (pauliRXBlock z) (pauliRZBlock z)
   446	
   447	/-- The answer constructor prescribed by each Pauli question type; this is the
   448	well-formedness part of `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   449	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   450	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   451	-/
   452	def validPauliAnswer {P : AdmissibleParams} (t : PauliType) (a : PauliAnswer P) : Bool :=
   453	  match t, a with
   454	  | .point _, .value _ => true
   455	  | .aline _, .alinePoly _ => true
   456	  | .dline _, .dlinePoly _ => true
   457	  | .pauli _, .pauliOutcome _ => true
   458	  | .pairW _, .bit _ => true
   459	  | .pair, .pairBits _ => true
   460	  | .ms (.constraint _), .msTriple _ => true
   461	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   462	  | _, _ => false
   463	
   464	/-- The axis-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   465	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   466	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   467	-/
   468	def pauliAlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   469	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   470	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   471	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   472	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   473	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   474	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   475	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   476	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   477	
   478	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   479	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   480	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   481	-/
   482	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   483	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   484	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   486	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   487	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   488	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   489	
   490	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   491	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   492	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   493	-/
   494	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   495	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   496	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   497	
   498	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   499	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    (match W with
   506	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   507	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   508	
   509	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   510	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   512	-/
   513	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   514	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   515	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   516	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   517	      (a * (match W with
   518	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   519	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   520	
   521	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   522	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   523	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   524	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   525	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   526	-/
   527	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   528	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   529	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   530	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   531	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   532	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   533	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   534	
   535	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   536	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   537	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   538	-/
   539	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   540	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   541	  open Classical in
   542	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   543	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   544	      if tA = tB then
   545	        decide (a = b)
   546	      else
   547	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   548	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   550	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   552	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   553	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   554	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   555	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   556	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   557	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   558	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   559	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   560	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   561	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   562	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   564	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   565	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   566	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   567	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true

   964	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   965	We now describe the question distribution of the game $\game^\pauli$, and show
   966	that it is a (typed) CL distribution.
   967	The question types in the game $\game^\pauli$ are
   968	\begin{equation}
   969	  \label{eq:pauli-type}
   970	  \type^\pauli= \bigl( \{\Point, \ALine, \DLine, \Pauli, \Pair \} \times \{X,Z\} \bigr)
   971	  \cup \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair\}\;,
   972	\end{equation}
   973	where $\type^\ms$ is the question type set of the Magic Square game defined in
   974	Section~\ref{sec:ms}.
   975	
   976	
   977	
   978	
   979	Before presenting the CL functions of the Pauli basis test, we first give an
   980	intuitive description of the question distribution of the Pauli basis test: a
   981	pair of questions $((\tvar_\alice, x_\alice), (\tvar_\bob, x_\bob))$ in
   982	$\game^\pauli$ can be sampled via the following procedure:
   983	
   984	\begin{enumerate}
   985	\item Sample a pair of types by sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice, \tvar_\bob)$ of
   986	  the graph $G^\pauli$ given in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli} uniformly at
   987	  random (including the self-loops).
   988	\item Sample the following uniformly at random:
   989		\begin{enumerate}
   990		\item (\emph{Points}) $u_\xpt,u_\zpt \in \F_q^m$,
   991		\item (\emph{Directions}) $s \in \F_q$, $v \in \F_q^m$,
   992	  \item (\emph{Qubit basis for (anti-)commutation}) $r_\xpt,r_\zpt \in \F_q$.
   993		\end{enumerate}
   994	\item For $w \in \AB$ and $W\in\{X,Z\}$,
   995		\begin{enumerate}
   996	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W)$, then set $x_w = u_W$,
   997	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\ALine, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s)$, where $u_0 =
   998	    L^\lnf_{e_i}(u_W)$, with $i = \chi(s)$ (see \Cref{sec:ld-game} for
   999	    definition of $L^\lnf$ and $\chi(s)$),
  1000	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\DLine,W)$, then set $x_w = (u_0,s,v')$, where $i =
  1001	    \chi(s)$, $v' = \pi_{i-1}(v)$, and $u_0 = L^\lnf_{v'}(u_W)$,
  1002	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Constraint_i$ for some $i\in\{1,\ldots,6\}$, then set
  1003	    $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1004	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Variable_j$ for some $j\in\{1,\ldots,9\}$, then set $x_w
  1005	    = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1006	  \item If $\tvar_w = \Pair$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1007	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pair, W)$, then set $x_w = (u_\xpt, u_\zpt, r_\xpt, r_\zpt)$,
  1008	  \item If $\tvar_w = (\Pauli, W)$, then set $x_w = 0$.
  1009		\end{enumerate}
  1010	\end{enumerate}

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on
  1116	$\type^\pauli \times V^\pauli \times \type^\pauli \times V^\pauli$ where
  1117	$(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice,\tvar_\bob,x_\bob)$ is sampled by first uniformly
  1118	sampling an edge $(\tvar_\alice,\tvar_\bob)$ from the graph $G^\pauli$ defined
  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

  1169	    On input $(\tvar_\alice,x_\alice, \tvar_\bob, x_\bob, a_\alice, a_\bob)$,
  1170	    the decision procedure $\decider^\pauli$ performs the following checks for
  1171	    $w \in \AB$:
  1172	    \begin{enumerate}[itemsep=2pt,parsep=2pt]
  1173	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1174	      \label{item:same-type}
  1175	      If $\tvar_\alice = \tvar_\bob$, accept iff $a_\alice = a_\bob$.
  1176	
  1177	    \item (\textbf{Low-degree}).
  1178	      \label{item:low-degree}
  1179	      Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,1)$. 
  1180	      \begin{enumerate}
  1181	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\ALine, W)$, accept if
  1182	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \ALine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1183	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1184	      	\item If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\DLine, W)$, accept if
  1185	      $\decider^\ld_{\ldparams}$ accepts $(\Point, x_w, \DLine, x_{\overline{w}}, a_w,
  1186	      a_{\overline{w}})$.
  1187			\end{enumerate}
  1188	    \item (\textbf{Consistency check}).
  1189	      \label{item:low-degree-consistency}
  1190	      If $\tvar_w = (\Point, W), \tvar_{\overline{w}} = (\Pauli, W)$, accept if
  1191	      $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}(x_w) = a_w$, where $g_{a_{\overline{w}}}$ is
  1192	      the low-degree encoding of $a_{\overline{w}} \in \F_q^M$ defined in
  1193	      Section~\ref{sec:ld-encoding}.

  1200	      (\ind_{m}(u_\zpt) \cdot r_\zpt) \bigr)\;,

  1229	We describe an honest, value-$1$ PCC strategy for the Pauli basis test.

  1231	
  1232	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:pauli-completeness}
  1233	  The Pauli basis test $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ has a value-$1$ SPCC strategy.
  1234	\end{lemma}
  1235	
  1236	\begin{proof}
  1237	  We begin by specifying the value-$1$ strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, E)$.
  1238	  The state is
  1239	  \begin{equation*}
  1240	    \ket{\psi} = \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M} \otimes \ket{\EPR_2}\;.

470	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   471	  -- The universal form preserves the source's zero-direction convention.
   472	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   473	    pauliPointBlock W point =
   474	        pauliPointBlock W line + t • coordinateDirection
   475	          (chiIndex P.toLdParams (pauliScalarBlock line)) →
   476	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   477	
   478	/-- The diagonal-line versus point relation used by `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   479	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   480	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   481	-/
   482	def pauliDlinePointCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   483	    (line point : PauliSpace P) (f : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   484	    (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   485	  ∀ t : PauliScalar P,
   486	    pauliPointBlock W point = pauliPointBlock W line +
   487	        t • pauliDirectionBlock line →
   488	      evalCoefficient f t = a
   489	
   490	/-- The raw Pauli-versus-point consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   491	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   492	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   493	-/
   494	def pauliPointPauliCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   495	    (point : PauliSpace P) (h : PauliRegister P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Prop :=
   496	  lowDegreeEnc h (pauliPointBlock W point) = a
   497	
   498	/-- The Pair/W consistency relation, including the one-sided gamma gate, from
   499	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   500	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   501	-/
   502	def pauliPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   503	    (z : PauliSpace P) (β : ZMod 2) (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   504	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   505	    (match W with
   506	    | .X => bits.1 = β
   507	    | .Z => bits.2 = β)
   508	
   509	/-- The point/Pair/W trace consistency relation from `def:pauli-win-predicate`,
   510	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   511	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   512	-/
   513	def pauliPointPairCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   514	    (z : PauliSpace P) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   515	  pauliPairGamma P z ≠ 0 ∨
   516	    fixedBinTrace P.model
   517	      (a * (match W with
   518	      | .X => pauliRXBlock z
   519	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β
   520	
   521	/-- The Point/Variable consistency clause of `def:pauli-win-predicate`.
   522	The check is gated by `gamma = 0` and only uses Variable 1 in the X basis or
   523	Variable 5 in the Z basis.  Blueprint
   524	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   525	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   526	-/
   527	def pauliPointVariableCondition (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   528	    (z : PauliSpace P) (j : Fin 9) (a : PauliScalar P) (β : ZMod 2) : Prop :=
   529	  pauliPairGamma P z = 0 ∨
   530	    (j = ⟨0, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .X ∧
   531	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRXBlock z) = β) ∨
   532	    (j = ⟨4, by decide⟩ ∧ W = .Z ∧
   533	        fixedBinTrace P.model (a * pauliRZBlock z) = β)
   534	
   535	/-- The Pauli win predicate, with constructor-shape rejection.  This is
   536	`def:pauli-win-predicate` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`,
   537	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   538	-/
   539	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   540	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   541	  open Classical in
   542	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   543	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   544	      if tA = tB then
   545	        decide (a = b)
   546	      else
   547	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   548	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   549	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   550	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   551	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   552	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   553	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   554	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   555	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   556	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   557	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   558	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   559	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true
   560	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   561	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   562	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   564	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   565	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   566	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   567	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true
   568	      | .ms (.constraint i), .ms (.var j), .msTriple β, .bit γ =>
   569	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   570	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   571	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))
   572	          else true
   573	      | .ms (.var j), .ms (.constraint i), .bit γ, .msTriple β =>
   574	          if ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j then
   575	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   576	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))
   577	          else true
   578	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   579	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   580	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   581	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   582	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   583	    else false
   584	
   585	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   586	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   587	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   588	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   589	-/
   590	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   591	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   592	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   593	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   594	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   595	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   596	  μ_prob := by sorry
   597	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   598	
   599	end
   600	
   601	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

347	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   348	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   349	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   350	-/
   351	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   352	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   353	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   354	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   355	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   356	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   357	  | msTriple (a : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
   358	  | pauliOutcome (a : PauliRegister P)
   359	  deriving DecidableEq
   360	
   361	/-- A finite sum code used only to construct the `Fintype` instance for the
   362	answer alphabet in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   363	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   364	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   365	-/
   366	abbrev PauliAnswerCode (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
   367	  PauliScalar P ⊕
   368	    ((Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   369	      ((Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P) ⊕
   370	        ((ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) ⊕
   371	          (ZMod 2 ⊕ ((Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ PauliRegister P)))))
   372	
   373	/-- The constructor-preserving finite-code equivalence for `PauliAnswer`.
   374	Lean-only infrastructure for `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint
   375	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin
   376	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   377	-/
   378	noncomputable def pauliAnswerEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   379	    PauliAnswer P ≃ PauliAnswerCode P where
   380	  toFun
   381	    | .value a => .inl a
   382	    | .alinePoly a => .inr (.inl a)
   383	    | .dlinePoly a => .inr (.inr (.inl a))
   384	    | .pairBits a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))
   385	    | .bit a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))
   386	    | .msTriple a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))))
   387	    | .pauliOutcome a => .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a)))))
   388	  invFun
   389	    | .inl a => .value a
   390	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePoly a
   391	    | .inr (.inr (.inl a)) => .dlinePoly a
   392	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))) => .pairBits a
   393	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a)))) => .bit a
   394	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inl a))))) => .msTriple a
   395	    | .inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr (.inr a))))) => .pauliOutcome a
   396	  left_inv := by
   397	    intro x
   398	    cases x <;> rfl
   399	  right_inv := by
   400	    intro x
   401	    cases x with
   402	    | inl a => rfl
   403	    | inr x =>
   404	        cases x with
   405	        | inl a => rfl
   406	        | inr x =>
   407	            cases x with
   408	            | inl a => rfl
   409	            | inr x =>
   410	                cases x with
   411	                | inl a => rfl
   412	                | inr x =>
   413	                    cases x with
   414	                    | inl a => rfl
   415	                    | inr x =>
   416	                        cases x with
   417	                        | inl a => rfl
   418	                        | inr a => rfl
   419	
   420	noncomputable instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Fintype (PauliAnswer P) :=
   421	  Fintype.ofEquiv (PauliAnswerCode P) (pauliAnswerEquiv P).symm
   422	
   423	instance (P : AdmissibleParams) : Inhabited (PauliAnswer P) :=
   424	  ⟨.bit 0⟩

   426	/-- The phase bit `γ(u_X,u_Z,r_X,r_Z)` from `eq:gamma-value`.  It uses the
   427	fixed trace selected by `P.model`, as required by the paper's fixed
   428	self-dual-normal representation.  Blueprint
   429	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`; paper origin
   430	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1198-1212`.

   432	noncomputable def gammaValue (P : AdmissibleParams)
   433	    (uX uZ : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   434	    (rX rZ : PauliScalar P) : ZMod 2 :=

   461	  | .ms (.var _), .bit _ => true
   462	  | _, _ => false

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
  1442	    \end{gather*}
  1443	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
  1444	\end{enumerate}
  1445	\end{theorem}
  1446	
  1447	We provide a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli} in \Cref{sec:qld-analysis}. 
  1448	
  1449	
  1450	The strategies described in the proof of \Cref{lem:pauli-completeness} and in the conclusion of \Cref{thm:pauli} are described in terms of qudit Pauli measurements and maximally entangled states defined over $q$-dimensional qudits. 
  1451	However, it is more convenient for our application of the Pauli basis test to
  1452	instead deal with \emph{qubits}.
  1453	In particular, we use the Pauli basis test in the ``introspection game'' of
  1454	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}, where the players are commanded to sample
  1455	questions according to a sampler $\sampler$ of a normal form verifier.
  1456	By definition of normal form verifier, $\sampler$ is a sampler over $\F_2$, and
  1457	therefore it is natural to use a test for qubit Pauli measurements.
  1458	
  1459	Since we use field sizes $q$ that are powers of $2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-binary}
  1460	shows that the conclusions of \Cref{thm:pauli} can also be described in terms of
  1461	testing for maximally entangled states over qubits and qubit Pauli measurements.

   653	\subsubsection{Bit string representations}
   654	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   655	
   656	As mentioned at the end of \Cref{sec:tms}, we sometimes treat the
   657	inputs and outputs of Turing machines as representing elements of a finite
   658	field, or a vector space over a finite field.
   659	We discuss some important details about bit representations of finite field
   660	elements and arithmetic over finite fields.
   661	
   662	In the paper we only consider fields $\F_{2^k}$ where $k$ is odd. 
   663	
   664	\begin{definition}\label{def:admissible-size}
   665	  A field size $q$ is called an \emph{admissible} field size if $q=2^k$ for odd
   666	  $k$.
   667	\end{definition}
   668	
   669	Elements of $\F_2$ are naturally represented using bits. 
   670	To represent elements of $\F_{2^k}$ as binary strings we require the
   671	specification of a basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.

   674	$k$-bit string corresponding to $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$.

   676	space over the prime subfield $\F_2$.

   678	natural binary representation of $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$ (which in turn is the
   679	\emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}).

   689	basis $\{e_i\}$.

   692	$\downsize(ab)$ of the product $ab$ is computed as

The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\\\\\\\\ndefinition equals itself.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\\\\\\\\nhow something was defined. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\\\\\\\\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Related issues\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\\\\\\\\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\\\\\\\\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\\\\\\\\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"precondition not met.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" Downstream\\\\\\\\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\\\\\\\\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\\\\\\\\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\\\\\\\\nfunction. A caller passing a\\\\\\\\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"the output\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" is\\\\\\\\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\\\\\\\\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\\\\\\\\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\\\\\\\\nprecondition failed.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\" The Lean should\\\\\\\\nmatch.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### How to spot it\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\\\\\\\\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\\\\\\\\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\\\\\\\\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\\\\\\\\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\\\\\\\\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\\\\\\\\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n```lean\\\\\\\\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\\\\\\\\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\\\\\\\\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\\\\\\\\n  match g with\\\\\\\\n  | some p => p.poly\\\\\\\\n  | none   => 0\\\\\\\\n```\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\\\\\\\\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\\\\\\\\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\\\\\\\\nthe preferred shape for new work.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nA signature passes the smell test if:\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\\\\\\\\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\\\\\\\\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\\\\\\\\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n### Related issues and patterns\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\\\\\\\\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\\\\\\\\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\\\\\\\\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\\\\\\\\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\\\\\\\\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\\\\\\\\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n---\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\\\\\\\\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\\\\\\\\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). 1	\section{Conditionally Linear Functions, Distributions, and Samplers}
     2	\label{sec:linear}
     3	
     4	\subsection{Conditionally linear functions and distributions}
     5	\label{sec:cl}
     6	
     7	We first introduce \emph{conditionally linear functions}, which are used to
     8	specify the question distribution for games considered in the paper in a way
     9	that the question distribution can be ``introspected'', as described in
    10	Section~\ref{sec:introspection}.
    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}
   131	
   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.
   281	
   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.

+needed by later formalization stages.

+`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
+The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
+and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.

+`s(a,b)` lies in `E`, including self-loops.  It is the inlined graph sampler of
+`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:553-563`;
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:984-1009`.
+The underlying graph-distribution definition is
+`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:65-82`.
+-/
+noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
+    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
+  Distribution.uniformOnFinset
+    (Finset.univ.filter fun ab : T × T => Sym2.mk ab.1 ab.2 ∈ E)
+
+/-- The graph sampler has unit mass whenever its edge set is nonempty. -/
+theorem graphDistribution_isProbability {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
+    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty) :
+    (graphDistribution E hE).IsProbability := by
+  sorry
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import Mathlib
+import MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Algebra.Pauli
+import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.Distribution
+
+/-!
+# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
+
+This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
+states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
+`Measurement` structure.
+
+## References
+
+The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
+`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
+The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/--
+A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
+pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
+-/
+structure Game where
+  QuestionA : Type
+  QuestionB : Type
+  AnswerA : Type
+  AnswerB : Type
+  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
+  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
+  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
+  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
+  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
+  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
+  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
+  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
+  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
+  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
+  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
+
+attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
+  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
+  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
+
+/--
+The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
+is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
+is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
+-/
+noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
+  M.postprocess Prod.fst
+
+/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
+`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
+-/
+noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
+    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
+  M.postprocess Prod.snd
+
+/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
+def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
+    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
+  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
+
+/--
+The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
+-/
+structure Strategy (G : Game) where
+  ιA : Type
+  ιB : Type
+  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
+  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
+  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
+  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
+  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
+  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
+  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
+  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
+
+attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
+  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
+
+/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
+the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
+-/
+def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
+  Matrix.kronecker A B
+
+/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
+functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
+using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
+/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
+action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
+noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
+  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
+
+/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
+`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
+private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
+    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
+  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
+    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
+  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
+  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
+
+/--
+The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
+probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
+-/
+noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
+    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
+      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
+
+/--
+The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
+strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
+for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
+intentionally not asserted here.
+-/
+noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
+  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

+import Mathlib
+import MIPStarRE.QPBT.Games.Defs
+
+/-!
+# Quantitative state and operator distances
+
+The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
+corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
+estimates to later proof stages.
+
+## References
+
+These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
+`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
+-/
+
+open scoped BigOperators
+
+namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
+
+open MIPStarRE.LDT
+open MIPStarRE.Quantum
+
+/--
+Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
+(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
+`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
+-/
+noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
+    [DecidableEq ι]
+    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
+  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
+
+/--
+Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
+is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
+with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
+-/
+noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
+    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
+    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
+  avgOver μ (fun x =>
+    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
+
+end MIPStarRE.QPBT

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.ParametersBase

     5	/-!
     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.
    11	
    12	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    21	
    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution
   101	
   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm
   117	
   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   127	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.

   129	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   130	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   131	than over a stored support finset. -/
   132	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   133	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   134	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   135	  rw [Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟 𝒟.weight 𝒟.outsideSupport]
   136	  exact h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one

   138	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   139	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   140	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   141	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   142	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one

   146	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   147	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by

   153	
   154	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
   155	whose total mass is one.

   157	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
   158	`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
   159	probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
   160	noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   161	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
   162	  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
   163	    (by
   164	      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
   165	        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
   166	      simp)
   167	    (by
   168	      intro a ha
   169	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   170	      simp)
   171	
   172	@[simp]
   173	theorem toPMF_apply {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   174	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :

   176	
   177	@[simp]

   180	    (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal = 𝒟.weight a := by

   182	
   183	/-- The associated PMF has zero mass outside the stored support of the project
   184	distribution. -/
   185	theorem toPMF_apply_of_notMem {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   186	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {a : α} (ha : a ∉ 𝒟.support) :

   188	  rw [toPMF_apply, 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   189	  simp
   190	
   191	/-- The project push-forward agrees with Mathlib's push-forward of the
   192	associated probability mass function. -/
   193	theorem toPMF_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   194	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   195	    (𝒟.map e).toPMF (h𝒟.map e) = (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).map e := by
   196	  classical
   197	  ext b

   199	  rw [ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg
   200	    (s := 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b))
   201	    (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   202	  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := 𝒟.support)]
   203	  · rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   204	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   205	    intro a ha
   206	    by_cases hea : e a = b
   207	    · have hba : b = e a := hea.symm
   208	      rw [if_pos hea, if_pos hba, toPMF_apply]
   209	    · have hba : b ≠ e a := fun hba => hea hba.symm
   210	      rw [if_neg hea, if_neg hba]
   211	  · intro a ha
   212	    by_cases hba : b = e a
   213	    · rw [if_pos hba, toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
   214	    · rw [if_neg hba]
   215	
   216	end Distribution
   217	
   218	/-- Average a scalar function against the stored finite support of a distribution. -/
   219	def avgOver {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) : Error :=
   220	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a
   221	
   222	namespace Distribution
   223	
   224	/-- The module-valued weighted finite sum associated to a finite-support `Distribution`,
   225	as a linear map in the averaged family.
   226

   228	operator averages.  It keeps the explicit support carried by `Distribution`,

     2	\label{sec:games}
     3	
     4	We introduce definitions associated with nonlocal games and strategies that will
     5	be used throughout.
     6	
     7	\subsection{Games and strategies}
     8	\label{sec:strat}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Two-player one-round games]
    11	  \label{def:game}
    12	  A \emph{two-player one-round game} $\game$ is specified by a tuple
    13	  $(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ where
    14	  \begin{enumerate}
    15	  \item $\cal{X}$ and $\cal{Y}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{question
    16	      alphabets}),
    17	  \item $\cal{A}$ and $\cal{B}$ are finite sets (called the \emph{answer
    18	      alphabets}),
    19	  \item $\mu$ is a probability distribution over $\cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$
    20	    (called the \emph{question distribution}), and
    21	  \item $D: \cal{X} \times \cal{Y} \times \cal{A} \times \cal{B} \to \{0,1\}$ is
    22	    a function (called the \emph{decision predicate}).
    23	  \end{enumerate}
    24	\end{definition}
    25	
    26	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]
    27	  \label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    28	  A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\strategy$ for a game $\game = (\cal{X},
    29	  \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    30	  \begin{itemize}
    31		\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ for finite
    32	    dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mH_A, \mH_B$,
    33		\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \cal{X}$, $A^x =
    34	    \{A^x_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_A$, and
    35		\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \cal{Y}$, $B^y =
    36	    \{B^y_b \}_{b \in \cal{B}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_B$.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	\end{definition}
    39	
    40	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]
    41	  \label{def:tensor-product-value}
    42		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\strategy =
    43	  (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$  with respect to a game $\game=(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A},
    44	  \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is defined as
    45	  \begin{equation*}
    46			\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \sum_{x,\, y,\, a,\, b} \, \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\,
    47	    \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^y_b\, \ket{\psi}\;.
    48	  \end{equation*}
    49		For $v\in[0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\strategy$ \emph{passes (or wins)
    50	    $\game$ with probability $v$ if} $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \geq v$.
    51	  The \emph{tensor product value} of $\game$ is defined as
    52	  \begin{equation*}
    53			\val^*(\game) = \sup_\strategy \val^*(\game, \strategy)\;,
    54	  \end{equation*}
    55		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\strategy$ for
    56	  $\game$.
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	
    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.

    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such

   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   205	  the players never return different answers when simultaneously asked the same
   206	  question.
   207	  As shown in~\cite{paulsen2016estimating} the condition for a
   208	  finite-dimensional strategy of being synchronous is equivalent to the
   209	  condition that it is projective, consistent, and moreover $\ket{\psi}$ is a
   210	  maximally entangled state.
   211	  (The equivalence is extended to infinite-dimensional strategies, as well as
   212	  correlations induced by limits of finite-dimensional strategies,
   213	  in~\cite{kim2018synchronous}.)
   214	\end{remark}
   215	\subsection{Distance measures}
   216	
   217	We introduce several distance measures that are used throughout.
   218	
   219	\begin{definition}[Distance between states]
   220	  \label{def:state-distance}
   221	
   222		Let $\{\ket{\psi_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ and $\{\ket{\psi'_n}\}_{n\in \N}$ be two
   223	  families of states in the same space $\mH$.
   224	  For some function $\delta : \N \to [0,1]$ we say that $\{ \ket{\psi_n} \}$ and
   225	  $\{ \ket{\psi'_n} \}$ are \emph{$\delta$-close}, denoted as $\ket{\psi}
   226	  \approx_\delta \ket{\psi'}$, if $ \norm{\ket{\psi_n} - \ket{\psi'_n}}^2 =
   227	  O(\delta(n))$.
   228	  (For convenience we generally leave the dependence of the states and $\delta$
   229	  on the indexing parameter $n$ implicit, writing e.g.\ $\ket{\psi}$ for $\ket{\psi_n}$.)
   230	\end{definition}
   231	
   232	\begin{definition}[Consistency between POVMs]
   233	  \label{def:consistency}
   234		Let $\mX$ be a finite set and $\mu$ a distribution on $\mX$.
   235	  Let $\ket{\psi} \in \cal{H}_A \otimes \cal{H}_B$ be a quantum state, and for
   236	  all $x\in \mX$, $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ POVMs.
   237	  We write
   238	  \begin{equation*}
   239	    A^x_a \otimes I_\bob \simeq_\delta I_\alice \otimes B^x_a
   240	  \end{equation*}

   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    \E_{x\sim \mu} \sum_{a\ne b} \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^x_b \ket{\psi}

   245	  \end{equation*}
   246	  In this case, we say that $\{A^x_a\}$ and $\{B^x_a\}$ are
   247	  \emph{$\delta$-consistent} on $\ket{\psi}$.
   248	\end{definition}
   249

     7	This module encodes the Boolean subcube by multilinear indicator polynomials

    31	abbrev Cube (m : ℕ) := Fin m → Bool

    37	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`).

    39	noncomputable def indicatorPoly {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ} (y : Cube m) :
    40	    MvPolynomial (Fin m) K :=

    43	/--
    44	The multilinear low-degree encoding of a coefficient string.  Polynomial
    45	representatives are used, as fixed by issue #0004, rather than quotienting by
    46	functional equality.  Blueprint: `def:low-degree-encoding`,

    48	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:832-897`.

    50	noncomputable def lowDegreeEncoding {K : Type*} [CommRing K] {m : ℕ}
